findings.diagnosis: The prompt under-detects short complements that actually complete the preceding predicate: it treats cuts before brief measures, temporal/locative phrases, directional words, or negating/infinitival complements as safe when they are essential to the clause's truth.
findings.evidence: en_us_44, en_us_767, en_us_292, en_us_360, en_us_733, en_us_113, en_us_1116, en_us_936 — each has a short (1–4 word) constituent immediately after the policy-kept cut that supplies a measure, time/place attachment, direction, or a negating/infinitival complement; cutting before it makes the fragment unfaithful or contradictory.
findings.type_predicate: Sentences where a 1–4 word constituent immediately following a potential cut is the syntactic complement of the immediately preceding verb or adjective and supplies a measure, temporal or locative attachment, direction, or a negating/infinitival that determines the clause's main truth-conditional content.

edit.text: Do not cut immediately before a short (1–4 word) complement that completes the preceding predicate (numeric measures, time/place phrases, directions, or negating/infinitival complements); treat such short continuations as essential to the clause.
